Around the winter of 1844-45, Miles Goodyear established a post here called Fort Buenaventura, after a mythical stream that early explorers thought drained the Great Basin region and emptied into San Francisco Bay. Settlement of the area did not begin until 1848, after Goodyear sold his property to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The settlement was first called Brownsville for James Brown, an early settler who represented the church in buying Goodyear's land and livestock. The name was changed to Ogden in 1850, when the General Assembly of Deseret created Weber County.
